title: Humility in Ministry
english: The high priest Moses, when God commanded him to send out the people, measured the power of human nature and saw that the ministry of preaching was greater. He said, 'I am weak-voiced and slow-tongued.'
Similarly, the blessed Jeremiah, when sent to prophesy, cried out, 'I do not know how to speak, for I am young.'
Even the saints, who speak such things, appear to be examples of piety, but this manner of fear is not small or harmless to the weak.

For God comforts us and encourages us to cast out fear, saying to Moses, 'Who gave a mouth to man, and who made one mute and deaf, seeing and blind? Is it not I, the Lord God? Now go, and I will open your mouth.'
And to Jeremiah, 'Do not say "I am young", for you will go to all whom I send you, and you will speak all that I command you.'
Therefore, I, a humble caller to the schema of priesthood, fearing the written 'Speak and do not be silent', necessarily come to write these things.
For God's judgment has well delivered our life, and towards the heavenly monasteries, the memory of our father Theophilus, who was bishop, has fallen to me, the least.
Hearing Paul write, 'Woe is me if I do not preach the gospel,' I am compelled by fear and weakness to proclaim.
Our holy things shine forth, and we are cleansed and purified, being called to a life of love and purity.
It is necessary to say to those still in wickedness to cleanse their hands and purify their hearts, for they have become diverse and multiform in sin.

The prophet will preach to those who have escaped the shame of sin and follow a life of love, saying 'Arise, Jerusalem, for your light has come and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.' (Isaiah 60:1)
For people have fallen into deep sin, overcome by the darkness of ignorance, and it is necessary for God to appear before us and save us.

We cry out to Him, 'Why have you withdrawn from us, Lord, and overlooked us in times of trouble?' (Psalm 44:23) for the Savior has not yet taken on our likeness, and is far from us according to the word of His incarnation.
The prophet Isaiah speaks about the existence of the Only-Begotten, and asks what generation will be able to describe it.

The Savior, born of a woman, appeared to us in our time of great affliction, to save the human being born of a woman, and having freed us from the bonds of death, teaches us to say: Where is your victory, death? Where is your sting, Hades? (1 Corinthians 15:55)

For he not only gives us the gift of resurrection, but also destroys the sting of Hades, that is, sin; he says: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you. (Luke 10:19)
This is one of the achievements of our Savior's presence, and it is a great comfort to us. Therefore, all dignity on earth is governed, and the darkness of ignorance has been dispelled.
The Psalmist, foreseeing this with the power of the divine Spirit, said: Justice and abundance of peace will arise in his days, until the moon is no more.
If we, being enemies, are reconciled to God through the death of his Son, an abundance of peace will arise for us.
When this happens, it is necessary for the moon to be abolished, that is, the ruler of night and darkness, called moon here in a figurative sense.
Therefore, such great and numerous lights shine for us, and the light of our divine festival shines, and again the bright festival draws us to itself.
It is clear that we should turn away from shameful things, as the wise advisor says: 'Wash and become clean, remove wickedness from your souls.' (Isaiah 1:16)
The Proverb writer's words also come to mind, 'There is a time for everything, and a season for every matter.' (Ecclesiastes 3:1)
If this is the case, then it is reasonable to agree that this time is an enemy of all wickedness, calling only those things that honor the divine law.
The judge of the contest of the righteous is God, who gives to the pious things that the eye has not seen, and the ear has not heard, and that have not entered the human heart.

Those who strive to contend in the present life, buying the title at great financial loss, and sweating in the contest, honor the winner with other wealthy prizes, but the gratitude is small, and the enjoyment only goes as far as the things of this life.
In contrast, the lovers of piety will find honor equal to their deeds, and having experienced the immense philanthropy of the Master, they will delight in goods beyond nature.
Let us then also call the lovers of piety to the annual contest of labors, and the prophet says that we should strive for virtue.
As we prepare to celebrate our holy feast, let us sound the trumpet in Zion, sanctifying a fast and proclaiming a solemn assembly.
This is a great and piercing call, a sacred trumpet that announces the presence of our holy feast.
The word of the Church is twofold, calling the ignorant to the correct understanding of divine doctrines and advising against the foolishness of works.
The trumpets are to be made of silver, symbolizing the brilliance and purity of the word. They guide us away from error and heresy, and towards the lawgiver's will.
As the prophet says, we must sanctify the fast and proclaim the healing.
How can we become workers of such things, fulfilling the divine command and striving to do the things that sanctify those who fast?
By avoiding evil, shunning shameful things, and following the brilliant and pure word of God, we can become the kind of people who truly celebrate the feast and serve the good God.
Let a disciple of Christ come among us and teach us the true manner of fasting, and we will listen to his words.
A pure and undefiled fast before God and Father is one that involves visiting orphans and widows in their affliction, and keeping oneself unspotted from the world.
It is not difficult to discover how and in what way we can fulfill these requirements.

For I believe that it is sufficient for those who are well-minded, and also the law of nature itself, teaches us to hate what seems to be contrary to divine commands, and persuades us to hold the will of the lawgiver in us.
This is the path that we must follow, and it is one that is guided by the principles of nature and the will of God.

title: Fasting
english: To truly find the grace of fasting, we must listen to Paul's command to put to death the earthly members, such as fornication, uncleanness, passion, and evil desire, and through which the remedy of fasting is also discovered.
This is not just about abstaining from certain foods, but about being pure and holy by rejecting the things that are contrary to our own mind and sending them away from our thoughts.
We must obey the holy one who says to cleanse our hands and purify our hearts, and to not nourish our mind with wicked pleasures.
By fleeing from the company of the unclean and showing ourselves to God through these actions, we can obtain the crown of righteousness.
It is good to abstain from excessive foods and to depart from the luxurious table, lest we, having indulged in excessive delicacies, arouse sin in ourselves.

For the flesh, being nourished and indulged, is difficult to control and resists the desires of the spirit, but when it is weak and not supported by excess, it necessarily gives in to the spirit, and this is what the blessed Paul teaches us, saying that even if our outer person is being destroyed, our inner person is being renewed day by day.

It is only fitting that the superior should conquer, and everyone would agree with this statement. The gain we derive from this is proportional to the harm that would result from the opposite, if we were to take the superiority of the better. Let us therefore rid ourselves of evil and avoid all indulgence in food, embracing instead the sobering practice of fasting, which is hostile to all sin.

The beauty of fasting is evident in the examples of the past, and I believe it is necessary to illustrate this to you. What was it that made John the Baptist, a man of great renown, so exceptional? It was not his birth or his upbringing, but rather his commitment to fasting and self-control. Similarly, Moses was prepared to enter the darkness and stand before God through his practice of fasting, which produces the idea of virtue in us. Fasting is the imitation of the angelic life, the source of sobriety, the beginning of self-control, and the destruction of lust. We see the power of fasting in the story of the three young men in Babylon, who, despite being offered luxurious feasts, preferred plain and unadorned food, and were thereby found to be formidable and unconquerable. But let us look at the fruit of this practice, and see how it can transform our lives.

The Ninevites were saved from a great threat by the preaching of a prophet, who announced that their city would be overthrown in three days. In response, the people took up fasting, which appeased the divine wrath and delivered them from the expected evils. Fasting has its own inherent signs of truth, and its beauty is more radiant when contrasted with its opposites.

The Hebrew people, while being fed in the wilderness, turned to strange desires when their leader Moses was absent, receiving the law from God on Mount Sinai. The people, taking the absence of their leader as an opportunity for foolishness, and neglecting the preceding order, turned to strange desires.

As it is written, the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play, which is a euphemism for fornication. Paul warns against such behavior, citing the example of those who fornicated and were killed by snakes. The people also despised the heavenly food of manna, remembering the food of Egypt and saying…

It would have been better for us to have died in Egypt, where we sat by the flesh pots and ate our fill. Through these experiences, the value of fasting has been clearly demonstrated to you, as I believe. Someone might object, saying that they know fasting is not without its benefits, but they also recognize that hard work can be harmful and even hostile to human nature.

Then how is it not shameful and most unseemly to desire better things and to make the acquisition of what is profitable a matter of great concern, but to be unwilling to become masters of the benefit that comes from them?

This is similar to how plants that grow from the earth have roots, and their growth cannot occur without them. In the same way, the beginning of joy is found through hard work and struggle, and it is through these efforts that joy arises and becomes apparent. We are left with two choices: either to decide not to work hard at all, which would result in our being deprived of all glory and honor, and being like the dead, taking no care for our own salvation, or to embrace the hard work that comes from fasting, and to justly gain the rewards that we would have otherwise lost.

Fleeing from the troubles of this world is, in fact, the best course of action for humans, as it allows us to avoid harm through small pains and sets us outside all loss and danger. On the other hand, not taking this path leads to great harm, making those who choose not to flee seem irrational. However, if we try to avoid small sufferings, we will inevitably fall into greater and more difficult ones. Therefore, it is only logical to choose the lesser pain, which is also the better option.

I would gladly ask those who think otherwise which they consider more troublesome: fasting or being punished for eternity. It seems to me that even they would agree that the hand should be cast into punishment. Since necessity brings us both options, why not choose the better one and plan our lives accordingly? For either we suffer and are freed from evils, or we avoid suffering and are condemned to unquenchable fire.

It is also worth noting that the use of pleasures is more delightful to those who have them when something unpleasant happens. This is evident in the case of those who are sick, for whom the good of health is more apparent, and those who are troubled by poverty and lack of necessities, who are more eager to gain because they are forced to seek what they do not have. The desire for pleasures becomes greater when they are absent, and this is how God, the master craftsman of all things, has arranged the universe, giving the sun to shine after night and after the sun, the night.

Through mutual exchange, the presence of each individual becomes more gracious and desirable, as they learn to appreciate the value of their own company. By neglecting the present moment and focusing on the future, they are able to anticipate and prepare for what is to come. The power of this mindset will ultimately prevail over both fasting and indulgence.

Fasting is not without its benefits, for it allows one to enjoy the pleasures of life more fully when the time is right. Therefore, let us embrace fasting as the mother of all good and every joy. However, it is unfortunate that the children of the Greeks, who consider themselves wise, despise this practice, while the Jews surpass all others in their devotion to it.

title: Hypocrisy and Disobedience
english: … They do not deny the novelty of wickedness, but they practice it so shamefully, as if they are superior when they are not caught. They are filled with all kinds of wickedness and bear all uncleanness within themselves, yet they make a pretense of virtue by clinging to the name of fasting alone.

Consider the example of the most ignorant and uneducated Pharisee, whom our Lord Christ describes in the Gospels (Luke 18:11-12) as praying in the temple. This Pharisee boasts about his fasting and tithing, yet he is full of pride and uncleanness within. He is like a whitewashed tomb, beautiful on the outside but full of dead bones and all sorts of uncleanness within (Matthew 23:27).

For they did not want to know the divine law, but also having trampled on the one given to them, they were disobedient and unrepentant. As a result, God reproaches them through the prophet, who cries out in frustration, asking to whom he should speak and testify, since the people's ears are uncircumcised and they are unable to hear. The word of the Lord has become a mockery to them, and they deliberately refuse to listen to it.

For those who sin voluntarily, the advice of what is beneficial is burdensome, and to those who want to live licentiously, self-control is not pleasant. This is similar to the state of those who are drunk, whose minds are confirmed in foolishness, and right thinking is removed. Likewise, those who are conquered by pleasure and have sunk into the depths of sin, having surrendered their sober mind to unclean passions, have evil firmly established within themselves, completely inclined towards it and looking at it, bound by this disease.

From the day your fathers came out of Egypt until this day, I have sent all my servants, the prophets, to you, but they have not listened to me, and they have not given ear, but instead they have stiffened their necks more than their fathers (Jeremiah 7:26). You alone have been shown the evil of your ancestors' deeds, and you have been born in unrighteousness, condemning the weaknesses of the law. You have been given the power to overcome, but you have chosen victory over all shame, and you have been allotted a vote. However, God, the judge of all, condemns you.

The prophet is told to lament the fact that the people have stiffened their necks, and the Lord says that he has rejected and despised the generation that did these things (Jeremiah 7:9-10). The sons of Judah did evil in his sight, setting up abominations in the house that bears his name, and building the altar of Topheth. They even denied their benefactor and considered idolatry more useful, giving sacrifices to the gods they had created for themselves.

Some people, driven by their passions, were devoting their minds to foreign desires, and they would seize the most beautiful mountain groves to offer sacrifices to the demons, invoking the nymphs, as the Greek poets called them, Hamadryads and Oreads. They were shameless in their desires, boasting about their actions, and causing great pain to the lawgiver. The prophet Jeremiah condemned such behavior, saying that the house of Israel had gone up to every high mountain and under every leafy tree to commit fornication, and yet they did not return to me (Jeremiah 3:2).

The Jews' harsh and unyielding choice is a testament to their refusal to be saved, as they always extend towards the worse, not knowing how to be self-controlled. They hate the ways of benefit and do not avoid the time of pleasure, not abstaining from it. This is evident in their failure to guard the beginning and their lack of humility towards the ambition of the Master.

Those who have the opportunity to know and be saved, yet neglect the things that are beneficial and do not consider the great love of humanity, will reasonably condemn themselves. For they have gone beyond all arrogance, having the chance to find release from punishment, but instead they have departed from sin and called upon themselves a heavier punishment, always adding to their transgressions. For who would not sin by advising the removal of the oil for these things? To those who are disposed in this way, it is more fitting to be punished than to not suffer evil.

The Lord of all says these things when he prevented the prophet from praying for them, saying, 'Do not pray for this people, and do not ask for them to be pitied, and do not approach me for them, for I will not listen' (Jeremiah 7:16). The people's sins are evident in their actions, as they provoke the Lord by offering sacrifices to foreign gods. The sons gather wood, the fathers kindle fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the army of heaven, so that nothing may be found outside of sin. They will rightly hear the Lord's judgment, for they have turned their backs on him, and he will turn his back on them, saying, 'For you have known my back, and I will turn my back on you, so that you shall not serve me as a priest. For you have known God's law, and I will forget your children' (Jeremiah 7:11-15).

The Israelites forgot God's law, and as a result, they suffered the consequences of their actions. The manner of punishment is always proportional to the magnitude of the sins committed, and those who have sinned must follow the path of sin in like manner. To be excluded from divine worship and to lose the memory they had from God is a terrible fate, one that is inaccessible to the foolish. The Israelites had been given a share of well-being and had lived without need, but they despised the Master's philanthropy and did not want to know the divine law.

Instead, they gave themselves over to all kinds of laziness and eagerly yielded to alien desires. They did not do what seemed necessary to the lawgiver, but rather set their own law according to their own will, and were guided only by their own decrees. Having such a mindset, they were prone to madness. The deed is a terrible thing, and inaccessible to the foolish. When those who least ought to have it appear to have acquired it, then a pretext for madness is found for those who possess it. The Israelites, having suffered this and having despised the Master's philanthropy, did not want to know the divine law, but rather gave themselves over to all kinds of laziness and eagerly yielded to alien desires, not doing what seemed necessary to the lawgiver, but rather setting their own law according to their own will, and being guided only by their own decrees. …
